_about: The Make system: each class makes a different kind of persistent world object. Every Make produces one record (creator, class, costs, owner, location, visibility, lifetime, events). The PDA previews and records; it resolves only what has a rule (a roll at a stated difficulty). Anything that changes the official world (a registry entry, a complaint outcome) is proposed and waits for a ruling. Heat comes from circumstances (where, with whose permission, who saw, what got sold where), never from the class. Status: draft, built on the First Edition rulebook (Downtime, Gear, Weapon & Armor Quality, Shade workings) and the World Anvil. Book prices are used for sale values where the book has one.

kinds.placed: A thing installed at a location. It keeps working there until it expires or someone removes it.
kinds.item: A thing you carry, use, give, or sell.
kinds.service: Work done for a specific person.
kinds.contract: An offer other players or NPCs can take up.
kinds.filing: Paperwork the city has to answer. Official changes wait for a ruling.
kinds.job: Work you take on and carry out in the world, on the Adyta clock.

public.name: Public
public.text: Anyone passing can see it. Best reach; easiest to find.

discreet.name: Discreet
discreet.text: Tucked away. Locals who look will find it.

hidden.name: Hidden
hidden.text: Only those who know where to look.

none.name: Nobody asked
none.text: Unauthorized. Each week there is a chance whoever watches the place finds it: Heat +1, a notice, and it is removed.

street.name: Sell on the street
street.text: Full price. Selling restricted work in the open is a witnessed sale: Heat +1.

fence.name: Through a fence
fence.text: 60% of the price. No questions, no Heat.

recipes.name: Doorway Ward
recipes.summary: A protective sigil set into a door or lintel, like the ward marks all through Ember Court.
recipes.effect: Anything hostile crossing this threshold spends an extra Action to do it, and you know it happened.
recipes.notes: Ward Keeper: keeps working between sessions without recasting; Maintain extends it a week at no Stress.

recipes.name: Alarm Sigils (3)
recipes.summary: Three sigil stickers. Stick one on a door or window and you know when it's crossed for the scene.
recipes.effect: One use: for a scene, you know when the marked door or window is crossed.
recipes.sizzle: Stuck on chrome or live tech it can SIZZLE: 1-in-6 something malfunctions.

recipes.name: Medkit, basic
recipes.summary: The book's basic medkit, built from parts instead of bought.
recipes.effect: Move the Wound Track up one step. One Action.

recipes.name: Gear Mod
recipes.summary: Rework a weapon or armor piece to Specialized quality.
recipes.effect: The piece gains one Tier 4 improvement (from the book's quality list).

recipes.name: Repair Order
recipes.summary: Fix someone's degraded armor or broken gear.
recipes.effect: Restore one degraded armor piece or broken item for the named character.

recipes.name: Signal Sticker Run
recipes.summary: A run of stickers across a district: a message, a symbol, a QR-ish thing that goes somewhere.
recipes.effect: While it's up: +1 die on Network and Streetwise in that district, and locals have heard your message.

recipes.name: Broadcast Spot
recipes.summary: A short pirate broadcast slot you can run for yourself or sell to someone.
recipes.effect: One message reaches a district's listeners. Unlicensed: Velvet Signal and Crownline both listen for these.

recipes.name: Route Sheet
recipes.summary: A hand-drawn sheet of public routes through a district.
recipes.effect: +1 die on Navigate in that district for whoever carries it.
recipes.notes: Public routes only. Threkktun never goes on a sheet.

recipes.name: Delivery Run
recipes.summary: Take a job off the board: pick it up, carry it across the city in Explore, drop it off before the deadline.
recipes.effect: Paid on arrival at the drop-off. Late pays half; very late (or a time-critical job that's late at all) pays nothing. Losing sealed cargo is Heat +1.

recipes.name: Delivery Slot
recipes.summary: Post your own open courier slot for crewmates or regulars to book. (Jobs off the city's board are Delivery Runs.)
recipes.effect: When it's booked and run, you're paid. Running it is a Side Job and may cost Heat depending on what's in the bag.

recipes.name: Cover Papers
recipes.summary: A cover identity good enough for a casual check.
recipes.effect: Passes a casual check once. It fails an ACR lookup, and a failed lookup is Heat +1.

recipes.name: Registry Change
recipes.summary: Propose a change to someone's official record.
recipes.effect: If the ruling goes your way, the Civil Registry now says what you made it say.
recipes.rulingNote: The city decides whether an official record changes. You propose; the session runner (or the GM) rules.

recipes.name: Market Listing
recipes.summary: Put something on the market for someone (yourself included) and take a cut.
recipes.effect: Each success adds 15% to the sale price. You take 10% of whatever it sells for.

recipes.name: Introduction
recipes.summary: Put two parties in a room who would never have found each other.
recipes.effect: The named character's next Work a Contact with that faction gets +2 dice.

recipes.name: APA Filing
recipes.summary: Paperwork prepared in advance, ready to throw at a notice.
recipes.effect: Attach to any appealable notice (yours or a crewmate's): that APA appeal rolls +2 dice.

recipes.name: Formal Complaint
recipes.summary: A complaint against an institution, through proper channels, with your name on it.
recipes.effect: If it lands, an institution has to answer for something on the record.
recipes.rulingNote: Whether an institution answers is a ruling. You file; the session runner (or the GM) decides what comes back.

recipes.name: Protection Contract
recipes.summary: Cover a person or a place for a week.
recipes.effect: The first threat against them this week meets you first. Lawful work: Heat only comes from what happens if it turns violent.

deliveries._about: Runner deliveries are real runs: take a job off the board, walk or tram it in Explore, and get paid when you arrive. A delivery is a Side Job (rulebook downtime action). Pay sits under the book's Minor job band because it's an errand, not a job.

cargo.name: Time-critical
cargo.text: Meds, a part, a key. Late is as good as never.

cargo.name: Sealed, no questions
cargo.text: Don't open it. Don't get stopped with it.
